issues.description: The problem statement specifies SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but both the template's example call and the solution implement acceptSupplyDelivery with only three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This discrepancy can confuse students about the required method signature and which parameters they must handle.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and implementations. Either update the problem statement to describe acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (removing the supplier name), or modify the template and solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update sample calls (e.g., in Main) accordingly so all artifacts share the same four-parameter signature.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery to accept four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) — see UML and textual description — but the template usage and the solution implementation use a three-parameter signature (ingredient name, price, quantity) and omit the supplier parameter. issues.suggestedFix: Either (A) update the solution and template to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update all calls (including Main) to pass the supplier name, or (B) revise the problem statement and UML to describe a three-parameter method (ingredientName, price, quantity). Choose one consistent signature and apply it across the problem statement, template examples, and solution code.
